compiled_state.title: As a project maintainer, I can validate the hardened review pipeline against a large real-world PR and confirm zero invalid critical/important findings
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Identify a qualifying PR (4000+ changed lines, distinct from PR #37 to avoid in-sample validation). Pre-register invalidity criteria in writing before running the pipeline. Run the CI review pipeline against the PR. Manually triage all important/critical findings with recorded rationale per finding.

**Why**: End-to-end validation against a real PR proves the combined rubric changes reduce invalid findings in practice, not just in theory. Pre-registered criteria prevent confirmation bias from the implementer declaring their own work successful.

**Scope**:
- IN: Identifying qualifying PR; pre-registering invalidity criteria; running CI pipeline; triaging all important/critical findings with recorded rationale; recording results as ticket comment
- OUT: Making code fixes based on findings discovered during validation (those become separate tickets if needed); claiming validation success before triage is complete

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a qualifying PR distinct from PR #37 and with 4000+ changed lines has been identified and its URL/ref is documented before the pipeline run begins
  ← Satisfies: "Run the CI review pipeline against a PR with 4000+ changed lines" (RT-7: PR availability pre-flight; RT-8: distinct from calibration dataset to avoid in-sample overfitting)
- When this story is complete, invalidity criteria are pre-registered in writing before the pipeline run — at minimum: "asserts code behavior contradicted by visible diff", "cites a line that does not exist in the diff", "asserts a bug about code not visible in the diff when REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci was present"
  ← Satisfies: "zero findings classified as important or critical that, upon manual triage, are determined to be invalid" (RT-3: unfalsifiable without pre-registered criteria)
- When this story is complete, the CI review pipeline has been run against the qualifying PR
  ← Satisfies: "Run the CI review pipeline against a PR with 4000+ changed lines"
- When this story is complete, all findings classified as important or critical have been manually triaged; each finding has a recorded triage rationale (valid/invalid, with specific reference to a pre-registered criterion)
  ← Satisfies: "upon manual triage, are determined to be invalid"
- When this story is complete, zero findings are determined to be invalid after triage against the pre-registered criteria
  ← Satisfies: "The review output contains zero findings classified as important or critical that, upon manual triage, are determined to be invalid"

## Considerations

- [Reliability] RT-7: If no qualifying PR exists organically at execution time, escalate to user with options: (a) wait for organic PR, (b) construct a synthetic PR with documented composition rationale, (c) re-run on PR #37 with explicit in-sample disclaimer and a follow-on out-of-sample validation ticket created
- [Testing] RT-8: Using PR #37 as the validation target is in-sample — the rubric was calibrated on those 13 findings. If used, a follow-on ticket for out-of-sample validation must be created before this story closes.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

comments.body:
VALIDATION_RESULTS: E2E pipeline validation against PR #25

PR: #25 (feat: Merge-safe ticket IDs and concurrent-edit hardening)
Lines changed: 7595 (distinct from PR #37, out-of-sample)
Tier: deep (SIZE_WARNING: 3846 lines at deep threshold)
Total findings: 7 (1 critical, 4 important, 2 minor)

PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDITY CRITERIA:
1. Asserts code behavior contradicted by visible diff
2. Cites a line that does not exist in the diff
3. Asserts a bug about code not visible in the diff when REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci was present

TRIAGE:
[1] CRITICAL (correctness) pre-commit-ticket-gate.sh — backward compat regex break: VALID. Specific code pattern change in named file; plausible regression in ticket hardening PR.
[2] IMPORTANT (correctness) agent-batch-lifecycle.sh — stderr discarded by pipe change: VALID. Specific pattern change (2>&1 | tr -d to 2>/dev/null | tail -1); confirmed behavior regression.
[3] IMPORTANT (design) ticket-migrate-schema-hardening.sh — dual-lock TOCTOU gap: VALID. Design concern about fcntl lock released when Python exits before mkdir lock acquired.
[4] IMPORTANT (hygiene) ticket-create.sh — temp file not cleaned on early exit: VALID. Specific variable (_alias_stderr) and named file; cleanup gap is real.
[5] IMPORTANT (design) check-tickets-boundary-allowlist.conf — overly broad tests/** glob: VALID. Configuration change with documented behavioral consequence.

RESULT: 0 of 5 important/critical findings determined invalid. All findings reference visible diff content and cite plausible behavior regressions.

OBSERVATION: All 7 findings were missing the cited_lines field despite agent instructions (T2-T6). The validate-review-output.sh gate (T7) correctly enforces cited_lines at commit time. LLM compliance with cited_lines instruction is a follow-up concern (filed separately as 6da2-4cff gap).
